Guidance & outlook: We are expecting that in Q2 going forward, maybe from August onwards, there could be a reduction of around INR1,000 to INR2,000 progressively in the coal cost -- in the imported coal cost on a… Got it.
So th at will become a beginning of selling -- of our efforts towards selling 32 million tonnes going forward.
And when it is 1.1 million tonnes this quarter, last year, we sold around 3 -odd million tonnes, although we are targeting a very high target of 8 million tonnes, let's see how far we can go.
Growth & demand: Indian steel industry, however, continues to enjoy robust demand for steel with consumption during quarter 1 '26 -'27, which has grown by more than 8% over CPLY.
The production, however, showed a muted slightly l ower growth of around 3% during this year -- during this quarter '26-'27.

Due to higher growth in imports as compared to exports, there was increase in imports as well as increase in exports and the net import for quarter 1 '26-'27 was to the tune of Steel Authority of India Limited July 28, 2026 around 0.4 million to 0.5 million tonnes as against maybe 0.3 million tonnes last year quarter 1.
Margins & costs: On the back of better realizations, sales turnover in creased by well over 1% as compared to previous year quarter 1.
EBITDA at INR4,356 crores showed for quarter 1 '26-'27 has a growth of more than 50% as compared to CPLY figure of INR2,925 crores.
EBITDA margin at 16.7% is one of the best since '21 -'22, when the steel market at that time was at its peak and coal price was at its bottom in '21 -'22.
Capex & expansion: Mostly, we had major capital repairs in IISCO Steel plant, Durgapur Steel Plant and also Bokaro Steel Plant, which were done in quarter 1 by design.
So far as capex is concerned, this year, we're planning a target of INR15,000 crores, and this is going to increase in the next 2, 3 years because our expanses are on.

You are right, actually by '28 -'29 when we start getting this thing production from IISCO steel plant expansion units, the variable cost will come down by around INR4,000 and fixed cost may go up around INR1,500 to INR2,000.
Balance sheet & cash: The company, however, remains very much committed towards increasing its sales volume, including inventory liquidation in the balance period of this year as we've done last year as well and also will be -- our endeavor will be to reduce the working capital borrowings.

And when we look at the borrowing po sition as on 30th June 2026 at the end of this quarter, we are almost at the same level as that of the beginning of this year in spite of the fact that the inventory has increased by 0.2 million tonnes.

What is the -- at present like in the last quarter, like the finance costs have declined and that remained as a major deleveraging supporting the overall debt and debt equity ratio has al so maintained to the multiyear low of 0.55.
Risks & challenges: On the other hand, the rising fuel cost led to inflationary pressures against raising the various expenditure heads.
The percentage of hard coking coal -- the percentage of soft coking coal is around 25% to 27%.
That means actually indigenous coking coal is 15%, then imported hard is 62% and imported soft is 23%.

Guidance & outlook: That is the kind of target, 10% on Steel Authority of India Limited May 16, 2026 the higher side, we're keeping it.
And the 0.6 million to 0.7 million ton guidance for RINL in FY27, that is on top of 22 million tons that we are seeing right now.

So going forward, in '26-'27, the capex guidance is INR15,000 crores, suppose it happens, INR14,000 crores, INR15,000 crores, we will see how to meet it from the internal accruals, because that is our personal target.
Growth & demand: Indian steel industry, when w e talk about that, Indian steel industry continues to enjoy robust demand for steel with the consumption during FY '25-'26, which has grown by almost 8% over the same period last year.

Company has posted highest ever sales volume at 19.9 million tons, almost like 20 million tons, which margina lly -- I mean, it is close to 20 million tons with a growth of 11% as compared to the previous year.

So on a like -to-like basis, purely volumes from SAIL, if I just remove RINL and NMDC volume this year, you are at about 18.8 mil lion tons of sales, and you're essentially saying that pure SAIL volumes will go from 18.8 million tons to upwards of 21 million tons in this year.
Margins & costs: Steel Authority of India Limited May 16, 2026 That is the reason why the borrowings have also come down by around INR8,150 crores in FY '25-'26, which has given sterling advantages in terms of finance cost to us.
Even the cost of borrowings has also come down from a level of 7.3% in the previous year to 6.2% this year.
Historically, wage revision has been around 15 %-odd or so.
Capex & expansion: And this year, we ar e expecting INR15,000 crores, and we'll be disbursing, because this will be partly for the debottlenecking Steel Authority of India Limited May 16, 2026 projects, partly for the AMR projects, as well as partly for the expansion projects of steel plant.
The capex for '26-'27 is INR15,000 crores, which is going to go up as we progress in our expansion.
And after that, this will go towards every year almost INR20,000 crores to INR25,000 crores, when expansion in these 3 plants will have its own effect.
Balance sheet & cash: There is a debt reduction of INR3,200 crores alone in quarter 4 of '25 -'26.
That's a very good sign, and it has resulted in huge inventory reduction and reduction in borrowings.

So that means in other words, actually, we will try to improve our profitability to a level in which the cash flows will be better, means the profitability plus depreciation will give us a cash flow, which probably will be able to take care of this year's capex to a large extent.
Risks & challenges: Regarding economic scenario, beginning with global economic scenario, the geopolitical situation in the Middle East has set the otherwise stabilizing e conomic scenario, again, bringing uncertainties and volatilities to all of us.
So that's not going to be a major challenge for us in quarter 1.
